Subject: Nightly ETL failure impacting morning dashboard loads

Hi Avery,

We noticed this morning that the nightly ETL job (tenant: mid-ops) failed to complete — several downstream dashboards show a partial-day snapshot and a number of transactions are missing for the 03:00–03:45 UTC window. This is affecting our reporting and finance reconciliation.

Quick details:
- Job ID: nightly-orders-2026-04-11
- Failure symptoms: job aborted with repeated 429/503 responses from the Redwoods API calls when writing embeddings (attached: job-run-stderr.log).
- First observed: ~03:06 UTC; job retried until 03:42 UTC then aborted.

Can you confirm whether this qualifies as a service degradation under our SLA and what the next steps are for evidence and compensation? We have a big board review on Tuesday and need an ETA for both a root cause and any credit calculation.

Thanks,
Sanjay Patel

Hi all — preliminary telemetry attached. Key observations from the control plane and serving logs:

- Impact window (serving surface): 2026-04-11T03:02:14Z — 2026-04-11T03:40:51Z (approx).
- Symptom: a burst of queued inference requests for mid-ops caused elevated tail latency and intermittent 429 responses when requests hit the per-tenant concurrency cap; several worker preemptions were observed in the same interval as cloud batch jobs reclaimed GPUs.
- Error pattern: repeated short-duration 429s followed by cascading retries from the orchestration layer; the orchestration retried aggressively which amplified queue pressure.

Attachments included: kv-eviction-trace-2026-04-11.zip (contains K/V cache eviction timestamps, host heartbeat logs, and per-shard queue depth samples) and a filtered raw trace (attached as job-run-stderr.log from customer).

Immediate recommendations:
- Evidence pull: we should bundle the tenant-level request-rate/time-series, the GPU preemption events, and the orchestration retry logs.
- Entitlement check: based on the window above, this looks likely to meet the "partial availability" threshold in section 3.2 of the contract, pending final correlation with the customer's job retries.
- Next step: schedule postmortem call and collect any additional orchestration logs from the customer to confirm retry amplification.

I'll start assembling the evidence packet and can produce a draft impact timeline by EOD.

David Kim
Senior SRE — Platform Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: kv-eviction-trace-2026-04-11.zip (archive)

From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>

Hi Sanjay — following up with the proposed plan and next steps.

Summary:
- Impact window: 03:02–03:41 UTC on 2026-04-11 (approx).
- Likely cause: queue saturation amplified by client-side retry behavior coincident with GPU preemptions.
- Entitlement: tentatively eligible as a partial-availability event; final determination requires correlating your orchestration retries with our request-level drops.

Proposed actions:
1) Evidence bundle: we'll produce a packet with per-token/request counts, host preemption events, and KV eviction timeline. Expect initial packet by Tue 04/13 17:00 PT.
2) Credit approach: we calculate the proportional credit using the contract's "affected-period" formula (pro-rata hours * monthly committed fee). We'll provide a worked example once the final impact window is agreed.
3) Postmortem call: can we confirm Mon 04/13 10:00 PT (30 min)? If that doesn't work, Wed 04/14 8:00 PT also available.

Action items for you: please attach the orchestration retry log (start/stop timestamps) and any controller-level retry backoff settings. That will help determine whether retry amplification changed the shape of the impact.

I'll include a short draft timeline and the partial credit calculation in the evidence bundle. Laura will own the entitlement sign-off and the final communication.

Thanks — really appreciate the quick report and patience while we validate.

Best,
Avery Johnson
Account Lead — Enterprise Customer Success
Redwood Inference
